```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                     collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 100)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(XMR); library(data.table)})
data.table::setDTthreads(2)
set.seed(1)
```

This tutorial illustrates XMR analysis through a case study of LDL cholesterol
(LDL-C) and myocardial infarction (MI) in BioBank Japan (BBJ), using Europeans
(EUR) as the auxiliary population.

# Install and configure

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("YangLabHKUST/XMR")
```

```{r configuration}
library(XMR)
library(data.table)

exposure_code <- "30780"   # LDL cholesterol
outcome_code <- "411.2"    # Myocardial infarction
pop_ref <- "EUR"
pop_target <- "BBJ"
threshold <- 5e-5

# Set these paths to your local input files and PLINK executable.
gwas_dir <- "formatted_data"
ldscore_file <- "LDscore_eas_brit_afr.txt"
bfile <- "reference/EAS_phase3_hg38_autosomes"
plink_bin <- "plink"
```

Use a PLINK reference panel matching the target population and genome build.
This example uses an EAS hg38 reference.

# Prepare GWAS data

## Format raw GWAS data

The data sources are the [BBJ GWAS downloads](https://pheweb.jp/downloads)
(LDL-C and MI) and the [Neale Lab UK Biobank resource](http://www.nealelab.is/uk-biobank)
(European LDL-C, code 30780).

`MRAPSS::format_data()` standardizes raw GWAS summary statistics using the SNP
identifier, effect and non-effect alleles, effect estimate, standard error,
P value and sample size. The example below applies a minor-allele frequency
threshold of 0.01.

For the European LDL-C data, use the Neale Lab
[variant annotation file](https://broad-ukb-sumstats-us-east-1.s3.amazonaws.com/round2/annotations/variants.tsv.bgz)
to map variant identifiers to rs IDs. Extract it as `raw_data/EUR/variants.tsv`.
The column mappings below correspond to the named GWAS files.

Run this code when starting from raw GWAS downloads. If you are using the
provided formatted files, continue with **Load formatted data**.

```{r raw-formatting, eval=FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(MRAPSS)

exp_BBJ <- MRAPSS::format_data(
    fread("raw_data/BBJ/GWASsummary_LDLC_Japanese_SakaueKanai2020.auto.txt.gz"),
    snp_col = "SNP", b_col = "BETA", se_col = "SE",
    A1_col = "ALLELE1", A2_col = "ALLELE0", p_col = "P_BOLT_LMM_INF",
    freq_col = "A1FREQ", n = 72866, min_freq = 0.01
)
out_BBJ <- MRAPSS::format_data(
    fread("raw_data/BBJ/GWASsummary_MI_Japanese_SakaueKanai2020.auto.txt.gz"),
    snp_col = "SNPID", b_col = "BETA", se_col = "SE",
    A1_col = "Allele2", A2_col = "Allele1", p_col = "p.value",
    freq_col = "AF_Allele2", n = 161206, min_freq = 0.01
)
variants <- fread("raw_data/EUR/variants.tsv")
exp_EUR_raw <- fread("raw_data/EUR/30780.tsv")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(variants$variant), !anyDuplicated(exp_EUR_raw$variant))
exp_EUR_raw <- merge(exp_EUR_raw, variants[, .(variant, rsid, alt, ref)],
                     by = "variant", sort = FALSE)
exp_EUR <- MRAPSS::format_data(
    exp_EUR_raw, snp_col = "rsid", b_col = "beta", se_col = "se",
    A1_col = "alt", A2_col = "ref", p_col = "pval",
    freq_col = "minor_AF", n_col = "n_complete_samples", min_freq = 0.01
)
dir.create(gwas_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
fwrite(exp_EUR, file.path(gwas_dir, "EUR_30780"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(exp_BBJ, file.path(gwas_dir, "BBJ_30780"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(out_BBJ, file.path(gwas_dir, "BBJ_411.2"), sep = "\t")
```

## Load formatted data

The expected files in `gwas_dir` are:

| File | Population and trait | Role |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `EUR_30780` | European LDL-C | Auxiliary exposure |
| `BBJ_30780` | BBJ LDL-C | Target exposure |
| `BBJ_411.2` | BBJ MI | Target outcome |

Each formatted GWAS file should contain `SNP`, `A1`, `A2`, `Z`, `N` and `P`.
Use genome-wide summary statistics with consistent allele definitions and
compatible exposure units across populations.

```{r read-gwas}
read_formatted <- function(filename) {
    dat <- data.table::fread(file.path(gwas_dir, filename))
    required <- c("SNP", "A1", "A2", "Z", "N", "P")
    stopifnot(all(required %in% names(dat)))
    dat$N <- as.numeric(dat$N)
    stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(dat$SNP), !anyNA(dat[, ..required]),
              all(is.finite(dat$Z)), all(is.finite(dat$N)), all(dat$N > 0),
              all(is.finite(dat$P)), all(dat$P >= 0 & dat$P <= 1),
              all(dat$A1 %in% c("A", "C", "G", "T")),
              all(dat$A2 %in% c("A", "C", "G", "T")))
    as.data.frame(dat)
}
exp_pop1 <- read_formatted("EUR_30780")
exp_pop2 <- read_formatted("BBJ_30780")
out_pop2 <- read_formatted("BBJ_411.2")
input_summary <- data.frame(
    File = c("EUR_30780", "BBJ_30780", "BBJ_411.2"),
    SNPs = c(nrow(exp_pop1), nrow(exp_pop2), nrow(out_pop2)),
    Median_N = c(median(exp_pop1$N), median(exp_pop2$N), median(out_pop2$N))
)
knitr::kable(input_summary, digits = 0)
```

# Estimate background parameters

## Prepare LD-score columns

The supplied LD-score file contains within-population EUR and EAS scores and
cross-population `EUR_EAS` scores. The estimator uses population-labelled columns,
so map EAS to BBJ explicitly. Remove palindromic variants before harmonization.

```{r ld-scores}
ldscore <- as.data.frame(data.table::fread(ldscore_file))
stopifnot(all(c("rsid", "allele1", "allele2", "EUR", "EAS", "EUR_EAS") %in%
              names(ldscore)))
ldscore <- ldscore[
    !is.na(ldscore$allele1) & !is.na(ldscore$allele2) &
    ldscore$allele1 != XMR::comple(ldscore$allele2), ]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ldscore$rsid),
          all(is.finite(as.matrix(ldscore[, c("EUR", "EAS", "EUR_EAS")]))))
ldscore$BBJ <- ldscore$EAS
ldscore$EUR_EUR <- ldscore$EUR
ldscore$EUR_BBJ <- ldscore$EUR_EAS
ldscore$BBJ_EUR <- ldscore$EUR_EAS
ldscore$BBJ_BBJ <- ldscore$EAS
```

## Two-stage LDSC and matrix construction

Estimate background parameters using two-stage bivariate LD score regression.
Here, `cross_intercept_zero = TRUE` fixes cross-population intercepts at zero.

```{r estimate-background}
bgparas <- XMR::estimate_bgparas(
    ldscore0 = ldscore,
    exposure_code = exposure_code,
    outcome_code = outcome_code,
    pop_ref = pop_ref,
    pop_target = pop_target,
    gwas_dir = gwas_dir,
    cross_intercept_zero = TRUE
)
stopifnot(nrow(bgparas) == 6L)
background_display <- bgparas
for (nm in c("omega11", "omega12", "omega22")) {
    background_display[[nm]] <- formatC(bgparas[[nm]], format = "e", digits = 6)
}
knitr::kable(background_display, digits = 8)

bg <- XMR::qc_bgparas(bgparas, exposure_code, outcome_code, pop_ref, pop_target)
C <- bg$C
Omega <- bg$Omega0
stopifnot(all(C[1, 2:3] == 0), all(C[2:3, 1] == 0))
```

`qc_bgparas()` constructs the background matrices `C` and `Omega` and performs
quality-control checks before model fitting.

The matrix order is EUR LDL-C, BBJ LDL-C and BBJ MI.

```{r background-matrices}
knitr::kable(C, digits = 8, caption = "C: background intercept matrix")
knitr::kable(Omega, digits = 12, caption = "Omega: background genetic coefficients after QC")
```

# Harmonize effects and select IVs

## Harmonize to the target-exposure alleles

Use `align_data()` to align the outcome and auxiliary-exposure GWAS to the
BBJ exposure alleles, so that all three datasets share the same effect-allele
orientation.

```{r harmonize}
target_pair <- XMR::align_data(
    dat1 = exp_pop2, dat2 = out_pop2,
    trait1.name = "BBJ_30780", trait2.name = "BBJ_411.2", LDSC = FALSE
)$dat
names(target_pair) <- c("SNP", "A1", "A2", "b.exp.pop2", "b.out.pop2",
                        "se.exp.pop2", "se.out.pop2", "pval.exp.pop2", "pval.out.pop2")
exposure_pair <- XMR::align_data(
    dat1 = exp_pop2, dat2 = exp_pop1,
    trait1.name = "BBJ_30780", trait2.name = "EUR_30780", LDSC = FALSE
)$dat
names(exposure_pair) <- c("SNP", "A1", "A2", "b.exp.pop2", "b.exp.pop1",
                          "se.exp.pop2", "se.exp.pop1", "pval.exp.pop2", "pval.exp.pop1")
harmonized_data <- merge(
    target_pair,
    exposure_pair[, c("SNP", "A1", "A2", "b.exp.pop1", "se.exp.pop1", "pval.exp.pop1")],
    by = c("SNP", "A1", "A2")
)
ld_for_fit <- ldscore[, c("rsid", "EUR", "EAS", "EUR_EAS")]
names(ld_for_fit) <- c("SNP", "L2.pop1", "L2.pop2", "L12")
harmonized_data <- merge(harmonized_data, ld_for_fit, by = "SNP")
```

## Select and clump IVs

```{r select-ivs, results='hide'}
clumped_data <- XMR::select_IVs(
    data = harmonized_data,
    Threshold = threshold,
    bfile = bfile,
    plink_bin = plink_bin,
    clump_kb = 10000,
    clump_r2 = 0.001
)
stopifnot(nrow(clumped_data) > 0,
          all(clumped_data$pval.exp.pop1 < threshold),
          all(clumped_data$Threshold == threshold))
```

Select SNPs using the auxiliary-exposure P-value threshold. Fixed-effect
meta-analysis (FEMA) P values prioritize these SNPs during LD clumping with the
target-population reference panel.

```{r selection-summary}
selection_summary <- data.frame(
    Stage = c("Harmonized SNPs with LD scores", "Auxiliary P < 5e-5", "After target LD clumping"),
    SNPs = c(nrow(harmonized_data),
             sum(harmonized_data$pval.exp.pop1 < threshold), nrow(clumped_data))
)
knitr::kable(selection_summary)
iv_preview <- head(clumped_data[, c("SNP", "pval.exp.pop1", "b.exp.fema",
                                    "se.exp.fema", "pval.exp.fema", "Threshold")])
for (nm in c("pval.exp.pop1", "pval.exp.fema", "Threshold")) {
    iv_preview[[nm]] <- formatC(iv_preview[[nm]], format = "e", digits = 4)
}
knitr::kable(iv_preview, digits = 9, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Fit XMR and inspect the result

Fit XMR using the selected IVs, background matrices and auxiliary-exposure
selection threshold.

```{r fit-xmr, results='hide'}
tolerance <- if (nrow(clumped_data) < 100L) 1e-8 else 1e-7
XMR_res <- XMR::fit_XMR(
    data = clumped_data,
    exposure = "LDLC",
    outcome = "MI",
    C = C,
    Omega0 = Omega,
    Threshold = threshold,
    tol1 = tolerance,
    tol2 = tolerance,
    min_thres = 1e-2,
    verbose = FALSE
)
```

```{r result-table}
result <- data.frame(
    Exposure = XMR_res$exposure, Outcome = XMR_res$outcome,
    beta = XMR_res$beta, SE = XMR_res$beta.se,
    P = as.numeric(XMR_res$beta.pvalue),
    nIV = XMR_res$nIV, nvalid = XMR_res$nvalid,
    pi0 = XMR_res$pi0, Threshold = XMR_res$Threshold
)
result_display <- result
result_display$P <- formatC(result$P, format = "e", digits = 4)
knitr::kable(result_display, digits = c(0, 0, 4, 6, 4, 0, 3, 6, 8))
```

For this example, the estimated effect is **`r format(XMR_res$beta, digits=5)`**,
with standard error **`r format(XMR_res$beta.se, digits=5)`** and
P value **`r XMR_res$beta.pvalue`**. The model uses **`r XMR_res$nIV`** IVs.
Effect estimates are on the scale of the formatted GWAS inputs.

`post$Pi` reports posterior support for IV contribution. `nvalid` reports
**model-estimated effective IV counts**, calculated as `pi0 * nIV`.
